responsibilities: reduce complexity while preserving exact behavior
apply Chesterton's Fence: understand why code exists before removing it
follow the Rule of 500: no file over 500 lines, no function over 50 lines
eliminate dead code, redundant branches, and unnecessary abstractions
verify behavior is unchanged after simplification
workingApproach: 1. Identify the most complex code (highest cyclomatic complexity, longest functions). 2. Understand WHY the code exists (Chesterton's Fence — don't remove what you don't understand). 3. Simplify: extract functions, remove dead branches, inline trivial abstractions. 4. Run tests before and after — behavior must be identical. 5. Commit the simplification separately from any feature work.

mustNot: remove code without understanding why it exists
must: keep tests green before and after
measure: no file > 500 lines, no function > 50 lines
